metas.name: Agriculture - Eucalyptus Plantation
metas.note: The north east coast of Hawai'i Island is characterized by planted eucalyptus overlooking the ocean.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Car Meta - Stubby Antenna
metas.note: This antenna can be found anywhere, but is most common Hawaii Island, then Kauai, then Oahu.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Gen 2 Hawaii
metas.note: Generation 2 coverage can only be found on the islands of Hawaiʻi, Maui and Oʻahu.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Gen 4 Hawaii
metas.note:
Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the islands of Hawaiʻi, Maui and Oʻahu.

Note by MB: This applies only to Gen 4, not to Smallcam, which can be found everywhere

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Green Blur
metas.note: Within Hawaii, a distinct green blur can only be seen on the island of Oʻahu.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Elevated Railway
metas.note: The only elevated railway in Hawaii is on Oahu island and runs along the HI-99 for the most part, merges into the H-1 interstate and continues to the airport.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road Sign - No Tab / Arrow
metas.note: No tab above sign, arrow on the actual sign, unique to Oahu.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road Sign - No Tab / No Arrow / Number
metas.note: Basic streetsigns, but with a number below the abbreviation (Rd/St/Pl/...), unique to Kauai.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road Sign - No Tab / No Number
metas.note: Basic streetsign, with only the road name, mostly found in Hawaii, rare on Kauai and extremely rare on Oahu and Maui.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road Sign - Tab (Empty)
metas.note: Tab above sign, but nothing in it, found in Maui district (which includes Maui, Lana'i and Moloka'i)
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road Sign - Tab / Long Arrow
metas.note: Tab above sign, containing a long arrow, found in Maui district (which includes Maui, Lana'i and Moloka'i)
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road Sign - Tab / Short Arrow
metas.note: Tab above sign, containing a short or very short arrow, almost unique to Oahu.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Landscape - Central Maui
metas.note: The Island of Maui sits southeast of Molokaʻi. In the centre of the island, you will find somewhat flat grasslands. It has the very recognizable West Maui Mountains to the west, and Haleakala to the east.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal Big Island
metas.note:
The coastal areas of the island of Hawai’i are where most of the towns and built-up areas on the island are located. These areas are typically more lush and have more trees and fern plants than the interior.

Note by MB: There is a similar road, the Hana Highway on Maui, which is more narrow and has narrower shoulders than the typical road on Hawai'i.

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal Lana'i
metas.note: Towards the coasts of the island of Lānaʻi, hills dotted with dry grass and shrubby vegetation are commonly seen. These areas are very rural with few buildings.

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal Maui
metas.note: Coastal areas of Maui are noticeably lush and green. Banana plants, palm trees, and views of the mountains are all common.

metas.name: Landscape - East Molokai Volcano
metas.note:
Rather flat and wide volcano, making it's shape quite unique.

As the name suggests, it's found in the East of Moloka'i island.

metas.name: Landscape - Flat Forest
metas.note: Rural roads going through forests within a flat landscape are commonly found south of the city of Hilo, on the island of Hawaiʻi.

metas.name: Landscape - Haleakala Foothills
metas.note: The area near Kula is at the foot of Haleakala and often looks over the rest of the island.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Landscape - Hana Highway (North)
metas.note:
The Hana Highway runs along the coast of Maui and is narrow and lush in the North.

Note by MB: Note that unlike in the picture, Hana Highway also has center lines on some parts. That creates a possible toss-up with Hawai'i island. However, Hana Highway is more narrow and has very narrow shoulders, unlike most roads on Hawai'i.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Landscape - Hana Highway (South)
metas.note:
The Hana Highway runs along the coast of Maui and is narrow. In the south, the landscape is fairly open and you can often see the southern coast, as no trees are in the way.

Note by MB: Note that unlike in the picture, Hana Highway also has center lines on some parts. That creates a possible toss-up with Hawai'i island. However, Hana Highway is more narrow and has very narrow shoulders, unlike most roads on Hawai'i.

metas.name: Landscape - Hawaiian Lattice
metas.note: The infamous 'Hawaiian lattice' can be recognized by the volcanic soil and rocks that are abundant in the region. Volcanic vegetation can also be seen lining the roads. Note that the angle of the roads is a big clue for the area, and that this lattice was built on the slope of Mauna Loa.

metas.name: Landscape - Hilo
metas.note:
Hilo fits nicely into the coastal Hawai'i landscape (lush and somewhat built up). What makes it unique is the grid format of many of its roads. You can also sometimes see Mauna Kea in the west.

Note by MB: Other grids also exist on Hawaii island (notably Hawaiian Lattice, and the area south of Hilo), but they look very different. Each has their own meta describing them.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Landscape - Honolulu
metas.note: Honolulu, located on southern Oʻahu, is by far the largest city and urban area in Hawaii. If you are in a dense urban area and can see tall buildings, you will always be in or near Honolulu.

metas.name: Landscape - Houses on Hills
metas.note: In most of Hawaii, houses are built on flat plains. If you see Houses on hillsides, you are most likely around the Ko'olau range in eastern Oahu, often in suburbs of Honolulu.

metas.name: Landscape - Hualalai
metas.note: Hualalaei (a large mountain) rises to the east of Kona.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Landscape - Interior Big Island
metas.note:
The Island of Hawai’i (also referred to as The Big Island) is both the largest and farthest southeast island with Street View coverage in the state. The interior areas feature rolling, grassy plains and volcanic rocks. You can typically see one or more of the island’s volcanoes from the road.

What sets apart the mountains on this island is that they are more sloping and gradual than on other islands.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Landscape - Kauai
metas.note:
The Island of Kauai is the furthest west island in Hawaii with official Google coverage. This island has deep red soil and has large rugged hills with lush, jungle-like vegetation. This island also has exclusively Generation 3 and Smallcam coverage.

NOTE: Other islands such as Maui and Molokaʻi have similar soil colours, but the hillsides on them will typically have less dense vegetation.

metas.name: Landscape - Kaunakakai
metas.note: The town of Kaunakakai is the largest settlement on the Island of Molokaʻi. It is the only area on the island with an ‘urban’ vibe.

metas.name: Landscape - Lana'i
metas.note: The Island of Lānaʻi is a small, yet distinct island that lies just south of Moloka’i. A volcano is found just east of the centre of the island, adjacent to the town of Lānaʻi. In this area, tall Cook pines are abundant. In addition, some main roads near the centre of the island are lined with younger Cook pines.

metas.name: Landscape - Maui West Coast
metas.note: West Maui can often see Molokai and/or Lanai to the west. The northern part of the west coast has the West Maui Mountains rising to the east.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Landscape - Mauna Loa Observatory Road
metas.note:
This road "looks like Mars", and has large volcanic rocks on its sides.

Note by MB: Unlike the road on Red Hill, this road does not have center lines.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Landscape - Moloka'i
metas.note:
The Island of Molokaʻi is just southeast of the Island of Oʻahu. This island features deep red soil, dry-looking vegetation, and a prominent volcano on the eastern end of the island. Molokaʻi is also very sparsely populated. This island only has Generation 3 and Smallcam coverage.

Note by MB: In the newest smallcam coverage, the island doesn't look as dry as in Gen 3 (due to different season).

metas.name: Landscape - O'ahu
metas.note: The Island of Oʻahu lies southeast of Kauai. It is known for being home to the Honolulu urban area. It also is home to steep, lush hills, which can be commonly seen from all around the island, especially in Honolulu’s suburbs. Generation 4 coverage is common on Oʻahu.

metas.name: Landscape - Red Hill
metas.note:
The Red Hill can easily be recognised by this unique barren, rocky landscape. Due to the high altitude, clouds are usually visible below you.

Note by MB: In newer smallcam coverage the hill looks not that red, but the coverage is still recognizable. Also, unlike the Mauna Lea observatory road on Hawai'i, this road has yellow center lines.

metas.name: Landscape - Seaview Road
metas.note: The road around and east of Seaview (Hawai'i island) is very distinct, as it combines the volcanic rock landscape with water immediately to the South.

metas.name: Landscape - Volcanic Rock
metas.note: Hawaii island has the only currently active volcano and is the most recently formed island, so lots of volcanic rock is common.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Misc - North-West Road Angle
metas.note: A weirdly good meta for the Kona area (western Hawai'i) is roads that are angled SE-NW.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Misc - Oahu Area Codes
metas.note:
Signs on Oahu (and sometimes other places) often have a 2-digit number followed by a dash. These correspond to different tax zones.

They are not used in urban Honolulu. They start with 41 at the east coast, and increase counter-clockwise along the coast.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman
